title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the cote and the notation. V is a real vector space with complexification V_C. φ_∞ is the real structure, i.e. complex conjugation: the 'Frobenius at infinity' generating Gal(C/R) inside Gal(Q̄/Q). V^{**} is the complement in V_C of a family Σ of real linear subspaces (lines/hyperplanes Δ, complexified to Δ_C). This is the model situation for moduli spaces M_{0,n} and configuration spaces, whose real points split into chambers. The page serves the study of how φ_∞ acts on the fundamental groupoid Π_1(V^{**}) when the base points are real (or conjugate) points, i.e. the archimedean part of the Galois action on the Teichmüller groupoid.

Definitions (left margin):
- l_{y,x}(t) = (x+y)/2 + e^{iπt}(x−y)/2 is the half-circle in the complex line through x and y, running from x (t=0) to y (t=1).
- φ_∞∘l_{y,x} is the conjugate half-circle.
- L_{y,x}(t) = t(x−y)+y is the straight segment.

Lemma 1. Take an oriented segment [x,y] and a real linear line Δ of V with Δ∩{x,y}=∅. The oriented half-plane condition is partly struck out; it apparently says x and y lie on the same side of Δ. Define the homotopy
f_{x,y}(s,t) = (1−s)·φ_∞∘l_{y,x}(t) + s·l_{y,x}(t).
For fixed t it runs along the vertical segment from the conjugate half-circle to the half-circle. The claim is that f_{x,y}([0,1]²) does not meet Δ_C.

Check. Write m=(x+y)/2 and r=(x−y)/2, both real, and let λ be a real linear form cutting out Δ. Then
f = m + cos(πt)·r + i(2s−1)·sin(πt)·r,
λ(f) = [λ(m)+cos(πt)λ(r)] + i(2s−1)sin(πt)λ(r).
- If λ(r)=0, then λ(f)=λ(x)≠0.
- Otherwise, vanishing needs (s=1/2 or t∈{0,1}) and λ(m)+cos(πt)λ(r)=0. That means the real point m+cos(πt)r of the segment [x,y] lies on Δ.
So f avoids Δ_C exactly when the real segment [x,y] avoids Δ. Moreover, at s=1/2 the homotopy is the straight segment itself, reparametrised.

Corollary. Take x,y ∈ V^{**} lying in the same real chamber, so that [x,y] avoids all of Σ. Then in Π_1(V^{**}) the half-circle path, its conjugate and the straight path L all coincide. The square formed by l_{y,x}, the vertical paths L_{x,φ_∞(x)} and L_{y,φ_∞(y)} (trivial for real points), and φ_∞(l_{y,x}) commutes. Hence φ_∞(l_{y,x}) = L_{φ_∞(y),φ_∞(x)}, i.e. complex conjugation fixes the canonical path class between real base points in the same chamber.
errors: As written, the hypothesis Δ∩{x,y}=∅ is insufficient. If the segment [x,y] crosses Δ at a real point p, then f_{x,y}(1/2, t₀) = p ∈ Δ_C for the t₀ with m+cos(πt₀)r = p. The correct hypothesis is [x,y]∩Δ=∅ (x and y on the same side of Δ), which the struck-out orientation/half-plane clause apparently tried to express.

Indexing and orientation conventions are inconsistent. The lemma names the homotopy f_{x,y} but uses l_{y,x}, and L_{y,x}(t)=t(x−y)+y runs from y to x, whereas l_{y,x} runs from x to y. This is harmless but sloppy.

For real x,y the vertical arrows L_{x,φ_∞(x)} are constant paths, so the square in the diagram is only meaningful as a formal statement of equivariance, or if non-real base points are intended. This is not clarified on the page.

ideas.what: Explicit straight-line homotopy between a half-circle path and its complex conjugate in the complement of a complexified real arrangement; it avoids Δ_C iff the real segment avoids Δ.
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation acting trivially on paths within a real chamber (Salvetti/Deligne-type cell paths)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Deligne (1972) for simplicial arrangements, Salvetti (1987) for complexified real arrangements

ideas.what: Action of φ_∞ = complex conjugation on the fundamental groupoid with real base points (chambers), as the archimedean component of the Galois action on Teichmüller groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation in GT / Gal(Q̄/Q) action on π_1(M_{0,n}) with real or tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; implicit in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses real structures and cells of M_{0,n}(R) only loosely

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, slightly mis-stated technical lemma about complex conjugation acting on paths between real base points in a complexified real arrangement complement. It fits the expected development of the Gal(C/R) part of the Teichmüller tower and contains nothing beyond folklore later formalised by Deligne, Salvetti and Drinfeld.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'e(t) = e^{iπt}' is consistent with l_{y,x}(t) = (x+y)/2 + e(t)(x−y)/2 going from x to y.
Line 'Alors f_{x,y}([0,1]×[0,1]) ne rencontre pas Δ_C' is confirmed by the image; it is Δ_ℂ, not Δ.
The orientation clause likely reads '(tel que l'orientation de Δ par le 1/2-plan contenant 0 soit [compatible avec celle] de x vers y)'.
Corollary: 'Si x,y ∈ V^{**} (et x,y ne ... i.e. x,y correspondant à des pts diff. de Σ^{*}) ... dans Π_1 V^{**}' — the superscript is ** in both places.
